spec.description: Animals on the move, from three open datasets: lesser black-backed gulls from Zeebrugge (INBO), jaguars across the Neotropics (Jaguar Movement Database) and sharks, tunas, whales, seals and turtles of the Pacific (TOPP, Animal Telemetry Network). Animated trails, distances and who went farthest.

options.content:
### About the data
Three open datasets of animals tracked by GPS or satellite, each read where it is published, through the stack's gateway, which keeps a copy for a month: none of them changes. DuckDB on the server reads each one once per visit and hands the browser a thinned copy; [Chaski](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/chaski) runs every query on the page there.

| Tab | Dataset | Publisher | Licence | Here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gulls | [LBBG_ADULT – Lesser black-backed gulls breeding in Belgium](https://zenodo.org/records/22083084) (2022–2025) | INBO, Research Institute for Nature and Forest; Movebank study, Zenodo | CC0 1.0 | One position per bird every two hours; kilometres from every fix |
| Jaguars | [Jaguar Movement Database](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.2dh0223), Morato et al. 2018, *Ecology* 99: 1691 | 20 research projects; Dryad, Zenodo copy | CC0 1.0 | One position per jaguar every two hours |
| Ocean | [IOOS ATN Trackline Database, Stanford Block Lab](https://atn.ioos.us/erddap/tabledap/stanford_import_ssm_public.html) (TOPP, 2002–2018) | Animal Telemetry Network, NOAA IOOS, on ERDDAP | Free use and redistribution, not for legal use | Tracks smoothed by a state-space model; one position per animal and day |

**Distances** are straight lines between fixes on a sphere, so they are a floor on what an animal travelled; fewer fixes, a lower floor. **The gulls' colony** is the median of all their positions in June. **Ocean longitudes** past 100°E are moved 360° west, so tracks across the date line draw as one line on a Pacific map.

**Not here:** the jaguars' sex, age and weight ship in the same archive as a spreadsheet misnamed `.csv`, which the reader cannot open from inside the ZIP. Movebank, the largest store of animal tracks, needs an account to download, so only studies also published on Zenodo or Dryad can join.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per bird of the year, the farthest travellers first, under a row
-- for all of them, whose click lets the picked bird go.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT bird, max(colony_km) AS far, min(latitude) AS south, sum(km) AS km,
         sum(fixes) AS fixes, min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1
  FROM $gulls
  GROUP BY bird
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All birds' AS label, '' AS bird, max(far) AS far, min(south) AS south,
         sum(km) AS km, sum(fixes) AS fixes, min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1
  FROM b
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, bird, bird, far, south, km, fixes, t0, t1 FROM b
)
SELECT label                           AS "Bird",
       round(far)                      AS "Farthest, km",
       round(south, 1)                 AS "Southernmost, °N",
       round(km)                       AS "Km flown",
       fixes                           AS "GPS fixes",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')        AS "First fix",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')        AS "Last fix",
       bird
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, far DESC

spec.description: Click a bird to follow it alone on the map and in the chart; All birds brings the others back.
spec.title: Birds

spec.rawSql:
-- How far each bird got from the colony, day by day: its farthest position
-- that day. The colony is the median of every position in June.
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 DAY, time) AS time, bird AS name, max(colony_km) AS value
FROM $gulls
WHERE $bird = '' OR bird = $bird
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY name, time

spec.description: Each bird's farthest position from the colony, day by day. The colony is the median of all the birds' positions in June, mid-breeding season. Hover a line to name its bird.
spec.title: Distance from the colony

options.content:
### Lesser black-backed gulls from Zeebrugge
Gulls GPS-tagged by [INBO](https://www.inbo.be/en) at their colony in the port of Zeebrugge, Belgium: up to 33 birds a year, a fix every few minutes, some wintering at home and some flying on to Iberia, Morocco or Mauritania. **Press play on the map's clock** to watch a year go by, each trail three days long; **click a bird in the table** to follow it alone; *All birds*, above the table, brings the others back. *Gull year* picks the year.

spec.rawSql:
-- Every bird, or the one picked in the table; trip_id groups a bird's
-- positions, one every two hours, into one trail.
SELECT bird AS trip_id, time, latitude, longitude, colony_km, km
FROM $gulls
WHERE $bird = '' OR bird = $bird
ORDER BY bird, time

SELECT count(DISTINCT bird)          AS "Birds",
       sum(fixes)                     AS "GPS fixes",
       round(sum(km))                 AS "Km flown",
       round(max(colony_km))          AS "Farthest, km"
FROM $gulls
WHERE $bird = '' OR bird = $bird

spec.description: Km flown adds up every fix to the next, before the map's thinning to one position every two hours. Farthest is from the colony.

spec.rawSql:
-- With a jaguar picked: the kilometres between its fixes, day by day.
-- Without: each country's median day, month by month.
WITH d AS (
  SELECT jaguar, country, time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 DAY, time) AS day, sum(km) AS km
  FROM $jaguars
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT day AS time, jaguar AS name, round(km, 2) AS value
FROM d WHERE $jaguar <> '' AND jaguar = $jaguar
UNION ALL
SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 MONTH, day) AS time, country AS name, round(median(km), 2) AS value
FROM d WHERE $jaguar = ''
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY name, time

spec.description: Kilometres between a jaguar's fixes, day by day, once a jaguar is picked; until then, each country's median day, month by month. Straight lines between fixes, so a floor on the real distance, and lower where collars fixed less often.
spec.title: Distance walked per day

options.content:
### Jaguars of the Neotropics
The [Jaguar Movement Database](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.2379): 117 jaguars GPS-collared by 20 projects from Sonora to Argentina between 1999 and 2016, most of them in Brazil's and Paraguay's Pantanal, where the map opens. Each trail is a week long; **press play** to run the clock, and **zoom out** for the other study areas, or **click one in the table** to fly there. **Click a jaguar** in its table to follow it alone and see how far it walked each day; *All jaguars* brings the others back.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per jaguar, the longest walkers first, under a row for all of
-- them, whose click lets the picked jaguar go.
WITH j AS (
  SELECT jaguar, any_value(study) AS study, any_value(country) AS country,
         min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1, sum(fixes) AS fixes, sum(km) AS km,
         median(latitude) AS lat, median(longitude) AS lng
  FROM $jaguars
  GROUP BY jaguar
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All jaguars' AS label, '' AS jaguar, '' AS study, '' AS country,
         min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1, sum(fixes) AS fixes, sum(km) AS km,
         NULL::DOUBLE AS lat, NULL::DOUBLE AS lng, NULL::DOUBLE AS per_day
  FROM j
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, jaguar, jaguar, study, country, t0, t1, fixes, km, lat, lng,
         km / greatest(date_diff('day', t0, t1), 1)
  FROM j
)
SELECT label                              AS "Jaguar",
       study                              AS "Study area",
       country                            AS "Country",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "First fix",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "Last fix",
       fixes                              AS "GPS fixes",
       round(km)                          AS "Km walked",
       round(per_day, 1)                  AS "Km per day",
       jaguar,
       round(lat, 4)                      AS lat,
       round(lng, 4)                      AS lng
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, km DESC

spec.description: Click a jaguar to follow it alone, and the map flies to it; All jaguars brings the others back. Km walked adds up the straight lines between fixes, a floor on the real distance.
spec.title: Jaguars

spec.rawSql:
-- Every jaguar, or the one picked in a table; one position every two hours
-- at most, as often as its collar fixed one. Coloured by country.
SELECT jaguar AS trip_id, study, country, time, latitude, longitude
FROM $jaguars
WHERE $jaguar = '' OR jaguar = $jaguar
ORDER BY jaguar, time

SELECT count(DISTINCT jaguar)   AS "Jaguars",
       sum(fixes)               AS "GPS fixes",
       round(sum(km))           AS "Km walked",
       count(DISTINCT study)    AS "Study areas"
FROM $jaguars
WHERE $jaguar = '' OR jaguar = $jaguar

spec.description: Km walked adds up the straight lines between fixes, so it is a floor: a jaguar walks more than the straight lines between its fixes, which some collars took hours apart.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per project, the largest first; a click flies the map to it.
SELECT study                                  AS "Study area",
       any_value(country)                     AS "Country",
       count(DISTINCT jaguar)                 AS "Jaguars",
       sum(fixes)                             AS "GPS fixes",
       min(year(time)) || '–' || max(year(time)) AS "Years",
       round(median(latitude), 4)             AS lat,
       round(median(longitude), 4)            AS lng
FROM $jaguars
GROUP BY study
ORDER BY "GPS fixes" DESC

spec.description: Click a study area to fly the map to it.
spec.title: Study areas

options.content:
### Ocean predators of the Pacific
[Tagging of Pacific Predators](https://gtopp.org/) (TOPP): 1,243 sharks, tunas, whales, seals, turtles and seabirds of 30 species tagged by the Stanford Block Lab from 2002 to 2018, one position a day, from the [Animal Telemetry Network](https://ioos.noaa.gov/project/atn/). Pick species in *Ocean species*; each trail is a month long. **Press play** on the map's clock, and **click a tag** in the table to follow one animal alone; *All tags* brings the others back.

spec.rawSql:
-- Where each species spends the year: the median latitude of its daily
-- positions, month by month, every year together.
SELECT month(time) AS month, species AS name, round(median(latitude), 1) AS value
FROM $ocean
WHERE $tag = '' OR tag = $tag
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY name, month

spec.description: The median latitude of each species' daily positions, month by month, every year together: the seasons of a migration.
spec.title: Latitude through the year

spec.rawSql:
-- The species picked, or the one animal picked in the table; one position a
-- day, longitudes past 100°E moved 360° west so the Pacific stays in one piece.
SELECT tag AS trip_id, species, time, latitude, longitude, km
FROM $ocean
WHERE $tag = '' OR tag = $tag
ORDER BY tag, time

-- Every species TOPP tagged, the most tagged first: what there is to pick.
SELECT species                                  AS "Species",
       taxon                                    AS "Group",
       tags                                     AS "Animals",
       positions                                AS "Positions",
       first_year || '–' || last_year           AS "Years"
FROM $ocean_species
ORDER BY tags DESC

spec.description: Every species in TOPP, picked or not: what there is to pick in Ocean species.
spec.title: What TOPP tagged

spec.rawSql:
SELECT count(DISTINCT tag)      AS "Animals",
       count(*)                 AS "Positions",
       round(sum(km))           AS "Km travelled",
       count(DISTINCT species)  AS "Species"
FROM $ocean
WHERE $tag = '' OR tag = $tag

spec.description: One position per animal and day. Km travelled adds up the straight lines between them.

spec.rawSql:
-- One row per animal of the species picked, the longest journeys first, under
-- a row for all of them, whose click lets the picked animal go.
WITH t AS (
  SELECT tag, any_value(species) AS species, min(time) AS t0, max(time) AS t1,
         count(*) AS positions, sum(km) AS km, max(latitude) AS north, min(latitude) AS south
  FROM $ocean
  GROUP BY tag
),
rows AS (
  SELECT 0 AS o, 'All tags' AS label, '' AS tag, '' AS species, min(t0) AS t0, max(t1) AS t1,
         sum(positions) AS positions, sum(km) AS km, max(north) AS north, min(south) AS south
  FROM t
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 1, tag, tag, species, t0, t1, positions, km, north, south FROM t
)
SELECT label                              AS "Tag",
       species                            AS "Species",
       strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "First position",
       strftime(t1, '%Y-%m-%d')           AS "Last position",
       positions                          AS "Positions",
       round(km)                          AS "Km travelled",
       round(north, 1) + 0.0              AS "Northernmost, °N",
       round(south, 1) + 0.0              AS "Southernmost, °N",
       tag                                AS tag_id
FROM rows
ORDER BY o, km DESC

spec.description: Click a tag to follow that animal alone on the map; All tags brings the others back.
spec.title: Tags

spec.description: The year of the gulls on the first tab; INBO publishes one file a year.
spec.label: Gull year
spec.name: year

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit and per year picked: the lesser black-backed
-- gulls INBO tags at their colony in the port of Zeebrugge (Belgium), from
-- the Zenodo copy of the Movebank study LBBG_ADULT (CC0), read through the
-- gateway's month-long cache. A year is up to 2 million GPS fixes, minutes
-- apart; the browser gets one position per bird every two hours, with the
-- fixes and the kilometres flown in those two hours, measured fix to fix.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT "individual-local-identifier" AS bird, timestamp AS t,
         "location-lat" AS lat, "location-long" AS lon
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/zenodo/records/22083084/files/LBBG_ADULT-gps-${year:raw}.csv.gz')
  WHERE visible AND "location-lat" IS NOT NULL AND "location-long" IS NOT NULL
),
leg AS (
  SELECT *, 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))) AS km
  FROM raw WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY bird ORDER BY t)
),
slot AS (
  SELECT bird, min(t) AS time, arg_min(lat, t) AS lat, arg_min(lon, t) AS lon,
         count(*) AS fixes, coalesce(sum(km), 0) AS km
  FROM leg GROUP BY bird, time_bucket(INTERVAL 2 HOUR, t)
),
-- The colony: the median of every bird's positions in June, mid-breeding.
colony AS (SELECT median(lat) AS clat, median(lon) AS clon FROM slot WHERE month(time) = 6)
SELECT bird, time,
       round(lat, 5) AS latitude, round(lon, 5) AS longitude,
       fixes, round(km, 3) AS km,
       round(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
         pow(sin(radians(lat - clat) / 2), 2)
         + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(clat)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - clon) / 2), 2))), 1) AS colony_km
FROM slot CROSS JOIN colony
ORDER BY bird, time

-- Server side, once per visit: the Jaguar Movement Database (Morato et al.
-- 2018, Ecology; CC0), 117 jaguars GPS-collared by 20 projects from Mexico to
-- Argentina, 1999 to 2016. Zenodo has it as a ZIP: GDAL reads the CSV inside
-- it by ranges of the gateway's month-long cached copy. Timestamps are local
-- and month/day/two-digit year. One position per jaguar every two hours, with
-- the fixes and the kilometres between fixes in those two hours.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT "individual.local.identifier (ID)" AS jaguar,
         trim(regexp_replace("study.name", '^[Jj]aguar_', '')) AS study,
         country,
         strptime(timestamp, '%m/%d/%y %H:%M') AS t,
         "location.lat"::DOUBLE AS lat, "location.long"::DOUBLE AS lon
  FROM ST_Read('/vsizip//vsicurl/http://feeds/zenodo/records/5001568/files/DataS1.zip/DataS1/jaguar_movement_data.csv')
),
leg AS (
  SELECT *, 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))) AS km
  FROM raw WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY jaguar ORDER BY t)
)
SELECT 'J' || lpad(jaguar, 3, '0') AS jaguar, any_value(study) AS study, any_value(country) AS country,
       min(t) AS time, round(arg_min(lat, t), 5) AS latitude, round(arg_min(lon, t), 5) AS longitude,
       count(*) AS fixes, round(coalesce(sum(km), 0), 3) AS km
FROM leg
GROUP BY jaguar, time_bucket(INTERVAL 2 HOUR, t)
ORDER BY jaguar, time

-- Server side, once per visit: what TOPP tagged, species by species, from the
-- same cached table as the tracks below.
SELECT species, taxon, count(DISTINCT tag) AS tags, count(*) AS positions,
       min(year(time)) AS first_year, max(year(time)) AS last_year
FROM read_csv('http://feeds/atn/topp.csv', header = false,
              columns = {'time': 'TIMESTAMPTZ', 'latitude': 'DOUBLE', 'longitude': 'DOUBLE',
                         'species': 'VARCHAR', 'tag': 'BIGINT', 'taxon': 'VARCHAR'})
GROUP BY species, taxon
ORDER BY tags DESC

spec.description: The species on the Ocean predators tab, the most tagged first.
spec.label: Ocean species
spec.name: species

spec.sql:
-- Every species TOPP tagged, the most tagged first.
SELECT species FROM $ocean_species ORDER BY tags DESC

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit and per choice of species: Tagging of Pacific
-- Predators (TOPP), the Stanford Block Lab's satellite and archival tags,
-- 2002 to 2018, as the Animal Telemetry Network publishes it on ERDDAP: tracks
-- already smoothed by a state-space model, about one position a day. Read
-- through the gateway's month-long cache. One position per animal and day,
-- with the kilometres covered since the previous one. West of 100°E a
-- longitude moves 360° west, so a crossing of the date line stays one line on
-- a Pacific-centred map instead of a stroke across the whole world.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT tag, species, taxon, timezone('UTC', time) AS t, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon
  FROM read_csv('http://feeds/atn/topp.csv', header = false,
                columns = {'time': 'TIMESTAMPTZ', 'latitude': 'DOUBLE', 'longitude': 'DOUBLE',
                           'species': 'VARCHAR', 'tag': 'BIGINT', 'taxon': 'VARCHAR'})
  WHERE species IN (${species:sqlstring}) AND lat IS NOT NULL AND lon IS NOT NULL
),
day AS (
  SELECT tag, any_value(species) AS species, any_value(taxon) AS taxon,
         min(t) AS time, arg_min(lat, t) AS lat, arg_min(lon, t) AS lon
  FROM raw GROUP BY tag, t::DATE
)
SELECT tag::VARCHAR AS tag, species, taxon, time,
       round(lat, 4) AS latitude,
       round(CASE WHEN lon > 100 THEN lon - 360 ELSE lon END, 4) AS longitude,
       round(coalesce(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
         pow(sin(radians(lat - lag(lat) OVER w) / 2), 2)
         + cos(radians(lat)) * cos(radians(lag(lat) OVER w)) * pow(sin(radians(lon - lag(lon) OVER w) / 2), 2))), 0), 2) AS km
FROM day
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY tag ORDER BY time)
ORDER BY tag, time
